fichas.title: Equestrian Facility: Functional Organization
fichas.summary: The facility is organized around self-contained buildings for horse accommodation, care, and feeding, with a covered riding area for all-weather activity. The arrangement of functions varies with the size and operational needs of the establishment. The diagram distinguishes functions under a roof or in a building, outside areas, people-only areas, areas shared by people and horses, and sight connections.
uses: Accommodating, caring for, and feeding horses
Riding and training in all weather
Connecting indoor and outdoor riding areas

fichas.title: Clear Dimensions of Riding Halls
fichas.summary: The page identifies a 20 × 40 m net riding space as the minimum, with larger 20 × 60 m spaces required for dressage from class M and eventing. Additional space is required at the sides and entrance, producing a stated gross arena size of 26 × 48 m. The page also illustrates riding-hall cross-sections and several structural arrangements.

fichas.title: Storage Space for Horse Feedstuffs
fichas.summary: A table compares the storage-space needs of oats, hay, and straw with daily feed requirements and stored quantities per horse. The table distinguishes storage forms such as long-stored, compressed, wired-bale, strung-bale, and chopped straw. Some table entries are difficult to associate unambiguously with individual rows, so they are not extracted as dimensions.
